ds: Poaching and trafficking of protected animals and plants and their products, such as ivory, rhino horn, pangolin scales, timber species and live animals. Financial signs include front companies mixing legal and illegal trade, payments across source, transit and demand countries, and use of trade documents falsified to pass inspection.

rat: Front import-export businesses, payments to officials and ground-level cash; sales advertised on social media and marketplaces with app/crypto payments.

ind.n: Trade in CITES-listed species with irregular permits
ind.cx: Customer exports or imports listed species with permits that do not verify, repeat or conflict with quantities.
ind.fp: Licensed breeders and traders deal in listed species.
ind.ds: Customer exports or imports listed species with permits that do not verify, repeat or conflict with quantities.

ind.n: Wildlife-related payments between source, transit and consumer countries
ind.cx: Flows between countries known as supply, transit and demand points linked to a small business.
ind.fp: Legitimate trade also uses these corridors.
ind.ds: Flows between countries known as supply, transit and demand points linked to a small business.

ind.n: Front businesses combining legal goods and wildlife products
ind.cx: Import-export firm in furniture, traditional medicine or seafood with unusually high-value shipments or inconsistent product descriptions.
ind.ds: Import-export firm in furniture, traditional medicine or seafood with unusually high-value shipments or inconsistent product descriptions.

ind.n: Payments to wildlife rangers, border officials or couriers
ind.cx: Payments to officials or low-income individuals around reserves and ports.
ind.fp: Payroll and local payments are normal.
ind.ds: Payments are made to officials, rangers or couriers around licences, inspections, reserves, ports or border clearances.
ind.cn: Payments to public officials to obtain permits or bypass controls

ind.n: Use of online marketplaces and social media payments for exotic animals or ivory
ind.cx: Sales of rare animals or carved items with payments through apps and unlabelled products.
ind.fp: Antique and pet markets exist lawfully.
ind.ds: Informal sellers or operators advertise online and collect payment through payment apps, crypto or unlabelled payments.
ind.cn: Illicit sales or services advertised on social media or marketplaces with app or crypto payments

ind.n: Cash intensive purchases by wholesalers at auctions or farms
ind.cx: Large cash buys from breeders, farms or auctions, then export.
ind.fp: Farms are cash-heavy in some regions.
ind.ds: Large or repeated cash payments to informal traders, producers or workers in extraction or supply chains.
ind.cn: Cash payments to informal suppliers or ground-level operators

ind.n: Transit via logistics hubs with changed consignee or false declarations
ind.cx: Reconsignment or splits in transit with different declared contents.
ind.ds: Reconsignment or splits in transit with different declared contents.

ind.n: Adverse media or enforcement links to wildlife trafficking
ind.cx: Customer or associates named in prosecutions, seizures or NGO investigations.
ind.ds: Credible negative news, enforcement notices or investigations link the customer, its owners or associates to criminal, corrupt or regulated-sector misconduct.
ind.cn: Adverse media on customer or associates

ctl.ds: Maintains lists of higher-risk goods, species and commodity codes, tags relevant transactions and triggers extra documentary checks and screening of descriptions. It focuses scrutiny on the goods most associated with abuse.

ctl.n: Licence and permit verification for regulated goods
ctl.ds: Validates licences, permits, certificates and authorisations with the issuing authority and compares their scope with observed activity or shipments. It prevents genuine permits being misused or forged permits being accepted.

Alerts on unusual countries, corridors, deposit locations and geolocation dispersion relative to the customer profile or on activity near designated risk regions. It focuses review on geographic anomalies.

ctl.n: Purpose and intended nature of relationship
ctl.ds: Captures and challenges the stated purpose of the account, expected activity, volumes and geographies at onboarding, creating a baseline against which later behaviour is judged. Vague or implausible answers prompt further enquiry or decline.

Compares declared unit prices, award values, fees and ancillary costs with reference databases, estimates and comparable contracts, and requires documented rationale for outliers. It detects over- and under-invoicing and inflated awards.

Tests whether an entity has real operations such as premises, staff, stock and contracts through documents, site or virtual visits, open-source footprint and shell-risk indicators. It helps identify shell and front companies with no genuine activity.
Tracks cases, outcomes, losses and false positives, routes concerns across fraud, sanctions and anti-corruption teams and feeds outcomes into tuning and appetite. It supports consistent handling.

ctl.n: PEP, relative and close associate screening
ctl.ds: Screens customers, beneficial owners, controllers, counterparties and their relatives and close associates against politically exposed person data at onboarding and on an ongoing basis. Matches trigger enhanced measures and senior approval.

Runs continuous screening of customers, owners, introducers, suppliers and counterparties against curated news, leaks, regulatory notices and enforcement releases, with reliability grading and identity disambiguation. It surfaces negative information that registers and lists do not carry.
Participates in sector, regulator and public-private forums and platform cooperation to receive and share typologies and indicators where lawful. It keeps scenarios current.
Reconciles cash, stock purchases, sales and exports with declared business activity to test whether deposits are plausible. It is used to identify unrecorded or injected cash.
Risk-based vetting of intermediaries, brokers, partners and suppliers covering ownership, experience, references, public-official links and selection rationale. It limits exposure through proxies.

ctl.n: Trade document review and consistency checking
ctl.ds: Trained staff and automated checks review goods, parties, routes, descriptions and codes across invoice, bill of lading and payment documents. It exposes mismatches and falsified paper.
